rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Said ibn Jubayr explains that these are houses that do not belong to the visitor.
rows.anchor: سعيد بن جبير في قول الله

rows.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
rows.claim: Maqatil says pre-Islamic Arabs used casual morning or evening greetings and entered without leave, disturbing household privacy; God replaced this with permission and greeting to secure modesty and cleanliness.
rows.anchor: مقاتل بن حيان قوله : يا ايها الذين امنوا

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda says Abdullah announced himself on entering a house by greeting and raising his voice.
rows.anchor: أبي عبيدة قال : كان عبد الله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses istiʾnās as asking permission to enter.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس قوله : لا تدخلوا بيوتا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, as related by Saʿid ibn Jubayr, says istiʾnās means asking permission and may be a scribal error in the written text.
rows.anchor: سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس قوله : حتى تستانسوا

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid explains istiʾnās as clearing one's throat or spitting to signal presence.
rows.anchor: مجاهد قوله : تستانسوا تنحنحوا تنخموا

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada prescribes seeking permission three times: announce yourself, allow the household to prepare, then accept either permission or refusal; if refused, leave without lingering at the door.
rows.anchor: قتادة حتى تستانسوا قال : هو الاستئذان ثلاثا

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report from the Prophet says a visitor can announce himself with glorification, takbir, praise, or throat-clearing so the household knows he is there; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: أبي ايوب قال : قلت يا رسول الله : هذا السلام

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Said ibn Jubayr explains istiʾnās as the step before asking permission.
rows.anchor: سعيد بن جبير في قول الله

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Said ibn Jubayr says the phrase puts the actions in forward order: greet the household, then ask permission; greeting precedes the request.
rows.anchor: سعيد بن جبير قوله : حتى تستانسوا وتسلموا

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima says that when entering an empty house one should say, Peace be upon us from our Lord, and peace be upon us and God's righteous servants.
rows.anchor: عكرمة في قوله : حتى تستانسوا وتسلموا

rows.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
rows.claim: Maqatil says visitors should greet first, then ask permission so residents can prepare; they enter if admitted and return if told to do so.
rows.anchor: مقاتل بن حيان قوله : حتى تستانسوا وتسلموا

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Said ibn Jubayr says the better course is permission and greeting rather than entering without leave, avoiding sin and giving residents warning.
rows.anchor: سعيد بن جبير في قول الله : ذلكم

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Said ibn Jubayr takes the reminder as the benefit of permission and greeting, by which one enters as God commanded.
rows.anchor: سعيد بن جبير في قول الله : لعلكم تذكرون

rows.speaker: أبو جهل
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq reports that Abu Jahl mocked the Prophet and his teaching that nineteen angels guard Hell, asking whether a hundred Quraysh could overpower one; this prompted the passage identifying the guardians as angels and their number as a test.
rows.anchor: أبو جهل يوما وهو يهزا برسول الله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says a pre-Islamic man might worship a white stone, then replace it with a better-looking stone and worship the new one.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس قوله : ارايت من اتخذ الهه هواه

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: A similar account of changing the stone worshipped is also reported from Saʿid ibn Jubayr.
rows.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير نحو ذلك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the person as a disbeliever who follows desire without God's guidance or proof; God led him astray according to prior knowledge.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس : ارايت من اتخذ الهه هواه قال : ذلك الكافر

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan al-Basri says such a person follows anything he desires.
rows.anchor: الحسن : ارايت من اتخذ الهه هواه قال : لا يهوي

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan also describes a hypocrite who makes desire his god and acts on whatever he wants.
rows.anchor: الحسن في قوله : ارايت من اتخذ الهه هواه

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the person does everything he desires, restrained by neither scruple nor piety.
rows.anchor: قتادة قوله : ارايت من اتخذ الهه هواه

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada glosses wakīl as a supporter or helper.
rows.anchor: قتادة قوله : وكيلا قال : ناصرا

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid explains every noble pair as plants of the earth eaten by people and livestock.
rows.anchor: مجاهد قوله : من كل زوج كريم قال : من نبات الارص

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿbi says people are like plants of the earth: those entering Paradise are noble, while those entering Hell are vile.
rows.anchor: الشعبي في قوله كم انبتنا فيها من كل زوج كريم قال : الناس من نبات الارض

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr explains karīm as good or beautiful.
rows.anchor: سعيد بن جبير قوله : كريم يعني حسن

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada is also reported to give the same gloss of karīm as good or beautiful.
rows.anchor: وروي ، عن قتادة مثل ذلك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas likens a sign to a sender's seal or garment, by which his household recognizes that a message is genuine.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس ان في ذلك لاية قال علامة الم تر إلى الرجل اذا ارد ان يرسل إلى اهله في حاجة

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: A similar explanation of the sign is also reported from Saʿid ibn Jubayr.
rows.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير نحو ذلك

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says Moses was called from the right side of Mount Sinai.
rows.anchor: السدي واذ نادى ربك موسى قال : حين نودي من جانب الطور

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the wrongdoers as disbelievers.
rows.anchor: الضحاك ، عن ابن عباس الظالمين يقول : الكافرين

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says Pharaoh pursued Moses with Haman at the head of an army of 1.7 million horses, none female.
rows.anchor: السدي قال : خرج موسى وتبعهم فرعون

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Anas reports that the Prophet said Noah was the first prophet sent; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: انس ان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : اول نبي ارسل نوح

rows.speaker: يزيد الرقاشي
rows.claim: Yazid al-Raqashi says Noah was named for his long lament over himself.
rows.anchor: يزيد الرقاشي ، قال : انما سمي نوحا لطول ما ناح

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Noah was sent at forty, preached among his people for 950 years, and lived sixty years after the Flood as people multiplied.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس قال : بعث نوح وهو لاربعين سنة

rows.speaker: عبيد بن عمير الليثي
rows.claim: Ubayd ibn Umayr reports that people strangled Noah until he fainted; on recovering he prayed for their forgiveness, and after generations of worsening defiance he complained to God.
rows.anchor: عبيد بن عمير الليثي انه كان يحدث انه بلغه انهم كانوا يبسطونه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the wage Noah disclaims as worldly goods.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس قوله : وما اسالكم عليه من اجر يقول عرضا

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن
rows.claim: Abd al-Rahman explains the statement as not asking the people for payment for the Quran.
rows.anchor: عبد الرحمن يقول في قول الله وما اسالكم عليه من اجر يقول : لا اسالكم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the warner as a warner of the Fire.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس نذير قال : نذير من النار

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan says Noah's opponents threatened to kill him; a similar gloss is reported from Zayd ibn Aslam.
rows.anchor: الحسن في قوله : لتكونن من المرجومين قال : تواعدوه

rows.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam is also reported to explain the threat as a promise of killing.
rows.anchor: عن زيد بن اسلم نحو ذلك

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada takes the threat literally as stoning with stones.
rows.anchor: قتادة قوله : لئن لم تنته يا نوح

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi explains being stoned as being abused with insults.
rows.anchor: السدي قوله لئن لم تنته لتكونن من المرجومين ، يقول : بالشتيمهة

rows.speaker: عبد بن عمير الليثي
rows.claim: A report from Abd ibn Umayr says Noah's people attacked and strangled him until he fainted; on recovering, he prayed, Lord, forgive my people, for they do not know.
rows.anchor: عبد بن عمير الليثي انه كان يحدث انه بلغه

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says ʿĀd lived in Yemen at al-Ahqaf, the sand dunes; Hud admonished and reminded them of the Qur'anic account, but they denied him and demanded punishment.
rows.anchor: السدي قال : ان عاد كانوا قوما باليمن بالاحقاف

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses rīʿ as every high place or eminence.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس قوله : اتبنون بكل ريع يقول : بكل شرف

rows.speaker: أبو صخر
rows.claim: Abu Sakhr explains rīʿ as mountains and elevated places on earth.
rows.anchor: أبو صخر اتبنون بكل ريع آية تعبثون قال : الريع : الجبال

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid gives one gloss of rīʿ as a small mountain pass.
rows.anchor: مجاهد في قول الله : اتبنون بكل ريع قال الريع الثنية الصغيرة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid also glosses rīʿ as a pass or valley.
rows.anchor: مجاهد بكل ريع قال : بكل فج

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Another report from Mujahid defines rīʿ as a pass between two mountains.
rows.anchor: مجاهد بكل ريع قال : فج بين جبلين

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi describes rīʿ as the road facing between mountains and hillocks.
rows.anchor: السدي اتبنون بكل ريع قال : الريع ما استقبل الطريق

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada glosses rīʿ as every road.
rows.anchor: قتادة في هذه الاية اتبنون بكل ريع قال : بكل طريق

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi is also reported to define rīʿ simply as the road.
rows.anchor: شريك ، عن السدي قال : الريع الطريق

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas is also reported to gloss rīʿ as the road.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس بكل ريع قال : الريع : الطريق

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid explains the structures built for amusement as buildings.
rows.anchor: مجاهد قوله : آية تعبثون بنيانا

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid gives an alternative explanation: the structures are dovecote towers.
rows.anchor: مجاهد قوله : آية قال : الاية اتخاذ ابرجة الحمام

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Ata describes them as frivolous buildings on every high and conspicuous place.
rows.anchor: أبيه عطاء واما بكل ريع آية تعبثون فيقال : بكل شرف

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses taʿbathūn as playing; the same gloss is reported from al-Dahhak and Qatada.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس تعبثون قال : تلعبون وروي ، عن الضحاك وقتادة مثل ذلك

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says no community's practices resemble ʿĀd's more than Muhammad's community, which likewise built conspicuous structures and took up imposing works.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد قال : ليس أحد اشبه فعالا بعاد من امة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says Salih was sent from al-Hijr.
rows.anchor: قتادة : ان صالحا بعث من الحجر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas recounts that Salih's people first believed, then abandoned Islam after his death; God revived and recommissioned him, they demanded a sign, and after the she-camel came they disbelieved, hamstrung it, and were destroyed.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس ان صالح النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بعثه الله إلى قومه

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima explains hāḍīm as ripe and soft; Qatada is also reported to give the same gloss.
rows.anchor: عكرمة في قول الله : ونخل طلعها هضيم قال : الهضيم الرطب اللين

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada is reported to explain hāḍīm as ripe and soft, like Ikrima.
rows.anchor: وروى ، عن قتادة نحو ذلك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains it as the fruit when it ripens and softens.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس في قوله : ونخل طلعها هضيم قال : اذا رطب واسترخي

rows.speaker: أبو صالح
rows.claim: A similar explanation is reported from Abu Salih.
rows.anchor: وروى ، عن أبي صالح نحو هذا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas also glosses hāḍīm as verdant or grassy.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس قوله : هضيم يقول معشبة

rows.speaker: أبو العلاء
rows.claim: Abu al-Ala calls it a ripe, soft date cluster; similar explanations are attributed to Abu Maysara, Yazid ibn Rashid, and Saʿid ibn Jubayr.
rows.anchor: أبي العلاء قال : ونخل طلعها هضيم قال : الهضيم المذنب الرطب

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan says the date cluster has no pit.
rows.anchor: عن الحسن ونخل طلعها هضيم فقيل : ليس فيه نوى

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the cluster scatters when touched.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد ونخل طلعها هضيم قال : الطلعة اذا مسستها تناثرت

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says it is when the date cluster separates and turns green.
rows.anchor: عن الضحاك ونخل طلعها هضيم قال : بطلع الطلع حين يتفرق ويخضر

rows.speaker: أبو صخر
rows.claim: Abu Sakhr describes the cluster as hāḍīm when it emerges from its sheath with the dates pressed together.
rows.anchor: أبو صخر ونخل طلعها هضيم قال : ما رايت طلع النخل حين ينشق

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid describes the cluster as breaking into pieces when touched.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد ونخل طلعها هضيم يتهشم تهشما

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the cluster crumbles and breaks apart when touched.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد ونخل طلعها هضيم قال : يتهشم ويتفتت اذا مس

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid compares ripe hāḍīm, which breaks when grasped, with dry hasīm, which is crushed; he also says it is so when it first appears.
rows.anchor: سمعت مجاهد يقول : ونخل طلعها هضيم قال : حين يطلع

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says a date cluster is hāḍīm when abundant fruit crowds and presses against itself.
rows.anchor: عن الضحاك في قوله : طلعها هضيم اذا كثر حمل الشجر

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Ata says obeying the messenger means following the Book and the Sunna.
rows.anchor: عن عطاء قوله : واطيعون قال : طاعة الرسول

words: وَتَذَرُونَ مَا خَلَقَ لَكُمْ رَبُّكُم مِّنْ أَزْوَٰجِكُم
rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says they abandoned women's vaginas for men's and women's anuses.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد وتذرون ما خلق لكم ربكم من ازواجكم تركتم اقبال النساء

words: مَا خَلَقَ لَكُمْ رَبُّكُم مِّنْ أَزْوَٰجِكُم
rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: When asked, Mujahid explains what God made suitable from their wives as the front, meaning vaginal intercourse.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد قال : سالته ، عن قول الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi explains what Lot's people do as having sex with men.
rows.anchor: عن السدي مما يعلمون يقول : ينكحون الرجال

none: Cross-reference to an earlier explanation only.

words: فَإِنْ عَصَوْكَ فَقُلْ إِنِّى بَرِىٓءٌۭ مِّمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ
rows.speaker: جعفر بن محمد
rows.claim: Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad says to disavow anyone who speaks of Abu Bakr and Umar except with good, citing the command to disavow their conduct.
rows.anchor: سمعت جعفر بن محمد يقول : تبرؤا ممن ذكر أبا بكر وعمر الا بخير

rows.speaker: محمد بن اسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq explains the command as being content with God in place of people.
rows.anchor: محمد بن اسحاق يعني : وتوكل على العزيز الرحيم اي : ارض به من العباد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains standing as rising for prayer.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس في قول الله : الذي يراك حين تقوم قال : تقوم الصلاة

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima says God sees the Prophet's standing, bowing, and prostration.
rows.anchor: عكرمة في قول الله : الذي يراك حين تقوم قال : يرى قيامه

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan says this refers to when the Prophet prays alone.
rows.anchor: الحسن يقول في قول الله : الذي يراك حين تقوم قال : حين تقوم اذا صليت وحدك

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says this means rising from bed or from one's seat.
rows.anchor: الضحاك الذي يراك حين تقوم قال : حين تقوم من فراشك

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima says God sees the Prophet standing and sitting among the people.
rows.anchor: عكرمة قال : الذي يراك حين تقوم معهم وتقعد

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says God sees the Prophet standing, sitting, and in all his states.
rows.anchor: قتادة قوله : الذي يراك حين تقوم يقول : الذي يراك قائما

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says God sees the Prophet wherever he is.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد : يراك حين تقوم اينما كنت

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan gives another gloss: when the Prophet is alone in private prayer.
rows.anchor: الحسن يقول : الذي يراك حين تقوم حين تخلو بها
